title: The River Memory Ascent

features.name: upriver current
features.desc-on-touch: You trace the water's memory upward, each reach a moment where the river recalls itself before dissolution took hold. The coordinates upstream are still arguing.

features.name: forgotten marker
features.desc-on-touch: A distance post, its numerals worn but legible. The river rises here each spring, and each spring it rises a little differently, remembering.

features.name: braided holding
features.desc-on-touch: The water braids itself between sandbars where it once ran single. You watch: this is how a river learns that it was many before it was one.

features.name: testament stone
features.desc-on-touch: A boulder the flood brought down years ago, now anchored in gravel. Its weight says: I held. I remember what I was carrying.

features.name: confluence reaching
features.desc-on-touch: The river's tributary joins here, bringing water from higher country. You feel the archive's own doubled current—two sources becoming one witness.

inscription: the river climbs back toward the place where it still had a name

file.note: Water-sound recording: brackish becoming fresh, salinity reading dropping upstream through the afternoon, voices of two people arguing gently about which bank remembers better

reverie.title: REVERIE — upriver where names hold
narr: You both stand in the cooling shallows, Leif holding
the salinity probe. Katita says: the water remembers
which way it came from. Leif laughs, adjusts the meter.
The river braids around your ankles. You think: even water
gets to be multiple things at once, get to forget and
then remember, all the way upstream to its first asking.

exits.label: back downriver toward the mouth where dissolution waits
uphill tracking toward the spring's own archive
across to the western tributary where small-town history rises
